pseudo_estimate_correction.what_was_wrong: Round 55 estimated R2-C3 prevalence as ~40-50% based on the proportion of recurrent patients who did NOT require surgery (70% of 57%). But 'not requiring surgery' is NOT equivalent to 'no objective findings.' The coder itself acknowledged this, then carried the estimate forward anyway.
pseudo_estimate_correction.what_is_corrected: R2-C3 prevalence = UNKNOWN. The number 40-50% is REMOVED from all downstream calculations. No sample-size calculation, power analysis, or study design uses this number.
pseudo_estimate_correction.why_this_matters: An unsupported estimate turned into a parameter is exactly the kind of convenience assumption that makes results look better than reality. The machine needed a number for powering, so it manufactured one from non-equivalent data. This is FORBIDDEN.
pseudo_estimate_correction.what_replaces_it: Two possibilities: (a) obtain patient-level data from existing studies to measure R2-C3 prevalence directly, or (b) if unavailable, design the study with a PREVALENCE SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS that reports required sample size across a RANGE of plausible prevalences (5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%) — without assuming any single value.

simulation_rename.what_it_IS: A test of whether the DISCOVERY ALGORITHM can recover a KNOWN synthetic structure under varying noise, missingness, and site heterogeneity. It tests ALGORITHM ROBUSTNESS, not clinical adequacy.
simulation_rename.what_it_is_NOT: It is NOT proof that n=1000 is clinically sufficient. The synthetic structure is PLANTED by the simulator — the real clinical structure is UNKNOWN. The simulation cannot establish the sample size needed for an unknown phenotype.
simulation_rename.correct_use: Use ARST to verify the algorithm works under stress BEFORE applying it to real data. Do NOT use ARST output as the clinical sample size.
simulation_rename.clinical_sample_size_status: NOT YET ESTABLISHED — requires externally anchored prevalence and effect size, which require patient-level data (see Step 3).

what_the_machine_can_do_once_data_arrive: Run Model D test: cross-tabulate (headache + ICP + papilledema + restenosis) to determine R2-C3 prevalence
If R2-C3 prevalence is >10%: proceed with sample-size calculation using the MEASURED prevalence
If R2-C3 prevalence is <5%: KILL R2-C3 (the phenotype is too rare to be a high-value invention target)
If R2-C3 prevalence is 5-10%: borderline — proceed only if the clinical harm justifies the study cost

the_decision_tree.if_data_FOUND: Run Model D → if R2-C3 exists and is prevalent → calculate clinical sample size → proceed to IRB
the_decision_tree.if_data_NOT_found: R2-C3 prevalence = UNKNOWN. Design study with PREVALENCE SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS (sample size calculated across 5-30% prevalence range). Acknowledge that the study may be underpowered if true prevalence is <5%.
the_decision_tree.if_data_found_and_R2_C3_is_TINY: KILL R2-C3. The 57% recurrence is mostly NOT the R2-C3 phenotype. Return to the phenotype decomposition and attack a different phenotype.
the_decision_tree.if_data_found_and_R2_C3_does_NOT_exist: KILL R2-C3 AND the entire latent-state hypothesis. The 'anomaly' was an endpoint artifact (Model D wins). Move to a completely different problem.

search_plan.cost_of_next_step_if_data_not_found: IRB + prospective study (expensive) — but ONLY after zero-cost options exhausted
